drivingQuestion: What does ben Beteira hold about a Paschal offering slaughtered on the morning of the 14th for its sake?
outcomeNote: R' Oshaya's reading falls to Rebbi's baraita; R' Yohanan's reading stands with three answers to R' Abbahu's challenge; the elder resolves R' Yirmeya's dilemma

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא: מַכְשִׁיר הָיָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא בְּפֶסַח שֶׁשְּׁחָטוֹ שַׁחֲרִית בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר לִשְׁמוֹ, דְּכוּלֵּיהּ יוֹמָא זִימְנֵיהּ הוּא.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «Rabbi Elazar says» that «Rabbi Oshaya says: With regard to a Paschal offering that one slaughtered» on the «morning of» the «fourteenth» of Nisan «for its sake, ben Beteira would deem» it «fit, as» he held that «the entire day,» not only the afternoon, «is its» designated «time.»

segments.he: וּמַאי ״כְּאִילּוּ״?
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And what» is the reason the mishna states that according to ben Beteira, a Paschal offering slaughtered on the morning of the fourteenth is considered «as though» it were slaughtered in the afternoon? This language seems to indicate that it does not have the same status as a Paschal offering actually slaughtered in the afternoon.

segments.he: אַיְּידֵי דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ ״כְּאִילּוּ״, אָמַר אִיהוּ נָמֵי ״כְּאִילּוּ״.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: «Since Rabbi Yehoshua says» the term: «As though» it were slaughtered on the thirteenth, ben Beteira «also says» the term: «As though» it were slaughtered in the afternoon. But in fact he maintains that there is no difference between a Paschal offering slaughtered on the morning of the fourteenth and one slaughtered in the afternoon.

segments.he: אִי הָכִי, אַדְּמִיפַּלְגִי בְּשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ – לִיפַּלְגוּ בְּלִשְׁמוֹ!
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «If so, rather than disagreeing» in the mishna «with regard to» a Paschal offering that was slaughtered on the morning of the fourteenth «not for its sake, let them disagree with regard to» one slaughtered «for its sake;» ben Beteira holds that it is fit, and Rabbi Yehoshua holds that it is unfit.

segments.he: אִי אִיפְּלִגוּ בְּלִשְׁמוֹ, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: אֲבָל בְּשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ – מוֹדֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְבֶן בְּתִירָא, הוֹאִיל וּמִקְצָתוֹ רָאוּי; קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «If» the mishna were to write only that «they disagree with regard to» a Paschal offering slaughtered «for its sake, I would say: But in» a case where it was slaughtered «not for its sake, Rabbi Yehoshua concedes to ben Beteira» that it is disqualified, even though it was slaughtered in the morning, «since» at least «part of» the day, the afternoon, is «fit» for its sacrifice as a Paschal offering. Therefore, the mishna «teaches us» that they disagree with regard to this case as well.

segments.he: וְהָכְתִיב: ״בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם״!
segments.en: The Gemara asks: How can ben Beteira claim that a Paschal offering may be slaughtered in the morning? «But isn’t it written:» “And the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall slaughter it «in the afternoon [bein ha’arbayim]”» (Exodus 12:6)?

segments.he: אָמַר עוּלָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב עִילַּאי: בֵּין שְׁנֵי עֲרָבִים.
segments.en: «Ulla, son of Rav Ilai, says:» Ben Beteira interprets the phrase bein ha’arbayim literally: «Between two evenings,» i.e., between the eve of the fourteenth and the night after the fourteenth. Accordingly, the Paschal offering may be sacrificed all day long.

segments.he: תָּמִיד, דִּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ: ״בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם״ – הָכִי נָמֵי דְּכוּלֵּי יוֹמָא כָּשֵׁר?!
segments.en: The Gemara asks: If so, with regard to the «daily offering, concerning which it is written:» “The one lamb you shall offer in the morning, and the other lamb you shall offer «bein ha’arbayim”» (Numbers 28:4), is «the entire day fit» for sacrifice «also?»

segments.he: הָתָם, מִדִּכְתִיב: ״אֶת הַכֶּבֶשׂ אֶחָד תַּעֲשֶׂה בַבֹּקֶר״, מִכְּלָל דְּ״בֵין הָעַרְבָּיִם״ – בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם מַמָּשׁ.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «There, since it is written: “The one lamb you shall offer in the morning,” by inference,» the term «bein ha’arbayim» is referring to the «actual afternoon.»

segments.he: אֵימָא חַד בַּבֹּקֶר, אִידַּךְ כּוּלֵּיהּ יוֹמָא!
segments.en: The Gemara counters: «Say» that «one» of the lambs should be sacrificed «in the morning,» and «the other» one can be sacrificed «all day.» Why is it evident from the requirement that one be sacrificed in the morning that the other must sacrificed in the afternoon?

segments.he: ״אֶחָד... בַּבֹּקֶר״ – וְלֹא שְׁנַיִם בַּבֹּקֶר.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: The clause «“One» lamb you shall offer «in the morning”» indicates that «two» lambs are «not» sacrificed «in the morning;» the other must perforce be sacrificed in the afternoon.

segments.he: נֵרוֹת, דִּכְתִיב ״בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם״ – הָכִי נָמֵי דְּכוּלֵּי יוֹמָא כָּשֵׁר?!
segments.en: The Gemara asks: With regard to the «lamps» of the Candelabrum, one should say the same, «as it is written:» “And when Aaron lights the lamps «bein ha’arbayim”» (Exodus 30:8). Is «the entire day fit» for lighting «also,» according to the opinion of ben Beteira?

segments.he: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דִּכְתִיב: ״מֵעֶרֶב וְעַד בֹּקֶר״, וְתַנְיָא: ״מֵעֶרֶב וְעַד בֹּקֶר״ – תֵּן לָהּ מִדָּתָהּ שֶׁתְּהֵא דּוֹלֶקֶת וְהוֹלֶכֶת מֵעֶרֶב וְעַד בֹּקֶר. דָּבָר אַחֵר: אֵין לְךָ עֲבוֹדָה כְּשֵׁרָה מֵעֶרֶב וְעַד בֹּקֶר, אֶלָּא זוֹ בִּלְבַד.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «There it is different, as it is written:» “To burn «from evening to morning”» (Exodus 27:21). «And it is taught» in a baraita: The phrase «“from evening to morning”» indicates that you must «allocate» the Candelabrum «its measure» of oil so «that it will burn from evening until morning. Alternatively,» the same verse can be interpreted as follows: «Only this rite is valid from evening until morning,» since all other rites must be performed during the day. Therefore, the Candelabrum is lit only at the end of the day.

segments.he: קְטוֹרֶת, דִּכְתִיב בָּהּ: ״בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם״ – הָכִי נָמֵי דְּכוּלֵּי יוֹמָא כָּשֵׁר?!
segments.en: The Gemara asks: With regard to the «incense,» one should say likewise, «as it is written with regard to it: “Bein ha’arbayim» he shall burn it” (Exodus 30:8). Is «the entire day also fit» for burning the incense according to the opinion of ben Beteira?

segments.he: שָׁאנֵי קְטֹרֶת,
segments.en: The Gemara answers: The «incense is different,»

segments.he: דְּאִיתַּקַּשׁ לְנֵרוֹת.
segments.en: «as it is juxtaposed with» the lighting of the «lamps» (see Exodus 30:8). Evidently, it is burned in the afternoon as well.

segments.he: הָתָם נָמֵי, כְּתִיב: ״שָׁם תִּזְבַּח אֶת הַפֶּסַח בָּעָרֶב״!
segments.en: The Gemara asks: Just as it is written explicitly that the Candelabrum must be lit in the evening, «there too,» with regard to a Paschal offering, «it is written: “There you shall sacrifice the Passover offering at evening”» (Deuteronomy 16:6). How can ben Beteira claim that it may be sacrificed all day long?

segments.he: הָהוּא לִ״יאוּחַר דָּבָר״ הוּא דַּאֲתָא, דְּתַנְיָא: יְאוּחַר דָּבָר שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ ״בָּעָרֶב״ וּ״בֵין הָעַרְבָּיִם״, לְדָבָר שֶׁלֹּא נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ אֶלָּא ״בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם״ בִּלְבַד.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «That» verse «comes to» teach a different halakha, that a certain «item should be» sacrificed «after» another item. «As it is taught» in a baraita with regard to the order of precedence between the Paschal offering and the daily afternoon offering: «An item,» i.e., the Paschal offering, «with regard to which» both the expressions: «“In the evening,” and: “Bein ha’arbayim,”» are «stated, should be» sacrificed «after an item,» the daily afternoon offering, «with regard to which only “bein ha’arbayim” is stated.»

segments.he: וּמִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי דְּאִילּוּ שָׁחֵיט לֵיהּ מִצַּפְרָא – אָמְרַתְּ זִימְנֵיהּ הוּא, וְכִי מָטֵי בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם – אָמְרַתְּ ״יְאוּחַר דָּבָר״?
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «But is there anything» comparable to ben Beteira’s suggestion, «that if one slaughters it in the morning, you say» that «it is its» designated «time» and it is fit; «but when afternoon comes, you say» that the «item should be» sacrificed only «after» the daily afternoon offering?

segments.he: אִין; דְּהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה – מִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁל מִנְחָה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁל מוּסָפִין.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «Yes,» there is a precedent; «as Rabbi Yoḥanan says:» If one did not recite the additional prayers of Shabbat, the New Moon, or a Festival, which should be recited in the morning, until it is time for the afternoon prayer, the «halakha» is that he should first «recite the afternoon prayer, and recite the additional prayers thereafter.»

segments.he: וּ״בֵין הָעַרְבַּיִם״ דִּכְתִיב גַּבֵּי קְטֹרֶת וְנֵרוֹת, לְמָה לִי?
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «But» if the term «“bein ha’arbayim”» is referring to the entire day, as ben Beteira maintains, «why do I» need those instances of the expression «that» are «written with regard to» burning «incense and» lighting the «lamps,» which are not performed all day?

segments.he: וְעוֹד הֵשִׁיב רַבִּי – תַּחַת בֶּן בְּתִירָא – לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: לֹא; אִם אָמַרְתָּ בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר – שֶׁאֵין מִקְצָתוֹ רָאוּי, תֹּאמַר בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר – שֶׁמִּקְצָתוֹ רָאוּי?!
segments.en: «Furthermore,» this interpretation of the opinion of ben Beteira is difficult, as «Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi «responded on behalf of ben Beteira to the statement of Rabbi Yehoshua» that a Paschal offering slaughtered not for its sake on the morning of the fourteenth of Nisan is fit, as though it were slaughtered on the thirteenth: «No, if you said» that this is the halakha «with regard to» the «thirteenth, as no part of» the day is «fit» for sacrificing the Paschal offering, «shall you» also «say» that this is the halakha «with regard to» the «fourteenth, part of which» is «fit» for sacrificing the Paschal offering? Since it can be sacrificed in the afternoon of the fourteenth, if it is slaughtered in the morning not for its sake, it is disqualified.

segments.he: וְאִם אִיתָא, כּוּלּוֹ רָאוּי הוּא!
segments.en: The Gemara concludes: «And if it is so» that a Paschal offering can be sacrificed throughout the day of the fourteenth, «all of it is fit,» not only part of it.

segments.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: פּוֹסֵל הָיָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא בְּפֶסַח שֶׁשְּׁחָטוֹ בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר שַׁחֲרִית, בֵּין לִשְׁמוֹ בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ, הוֹאִיל וּמִקְצָתוֹ רָאוּי.
segments.en: «Rather,» Rabbi Oshaya’s interpretation of ben Beteira’s opinion is rejected. Instead, «Rabbi Yoḥanan says: With regard to a Paschal offering that one slaughtered on the fourteenth in the morning, ben Beteira would deem» it «unfit, whether» it was slaughtered «for its sake or not for its sake.» It is unfit even if it was slaughtered not for its sake, «since part of» the day is «fit» for its sacrifice as a Paschal offering.

segments.he: מְגַדֵּף בַּהּ רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: אִם כֵּן, פֶּסַח כָּשֵׁר לְבֶן בְּתִירָא – הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ? אִי דְּאַפְרְשֵׁיהּ הָאִידָּנָא – דָּחוּי מֵעִיקָּרוֹ הוּא, וְאִי דְּאַפְרְשִׁינְהוּ מֵאֶתְמוֹל – נִרְאֶה וְנִדְחֶה הוּא!
segments.en: «Rabbi Abbahu ridiculed [megaddef ]» this interpretation: «If so, how can you find a fit Paschal offering according to ben Beteira? If» its owner «designated» an animal «now,» on the morning of the fourteenth, as a Paschal offering, «it is disqualified from the outset,» as it cannot be sacrificed at all, either for its sake or not for its sake. «And» even «if» its owner «designated it the previous day,» when it was fit to be sacrificed not for its sake, «it was fit and» then «disqualified» the next morning, when it was no longer fit to be sacrificed until the afternoon. Once an offering is disqualified, it can no longer become fit.

segments.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: תְּהֵא לְאַחַר חֲצוֹת.
segments.en: «Rather, Rabbi Abbahu says: Let» the Paschal offering «be» fit when it is designated on the fourteenth «after noon,» when it may already be sacrificed as a Paschal offering.

segments.he: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא מִצַּפְרָא – אֵין מְחוּסַּר זְמַן לְבוֹ בַּיּוֹם.
segments.en: «Abaye says: You» may «even say» that it is fit if designated «in the morning,» as an offering is «not» disqualified due to the fact that it is an offering «whose time has not yet» arrived if its time will arrive «on that same day.»

segments.he: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא מֵאוּרְתָּא – לַיְלָה אֵין מְחוּסָּר זְמַן; דְּתָנֵי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: לֵיל שְׁמִינִי נִכְנָס לַדִּיר לְהִתְעַשֵּׂר.
segments.en: «Rav Pappa says: You» may «even say» that it is fit if designated «from» the previous «night,» as an offering that was designated at «night» and may be sacrificed the following day is «not» considered an offering «whose time has not yet» arrived, «as it is taught in the school of Rabbi Yishmael:» Although an animal is unfit for sacrifice until its eighth day, on the «night» before its «eighth» day it may already «enter the den to be tithed.»

segments.he: וְכִדְרַבִּי אַפְטוֹרִיקִי, דְּרַבִּי אַפְטוֹרִיקִי רָמֵי: כְּתִיב ״וְהָיָה שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תַּחַת אִמּוֹ״ – הָא לַיְלָה חֲזֵי; וּכְתִיב ״וּמִיּוֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי וָהָלְאָה יֵרָצֶה״ – הָא לַיְלָה לָא חֲזֵי!
segments.en: «And» this is «in accordance with» the statement «of Rabbi Appetoriki, as Rabbi Appetoriki raises a contradiction: It is written:» “When a bull or a sheep or a goat is born, «then it shall be seven days with its mother”» (Leviticus 22:27); «consequently,» on the following «night,» i.e., the night before the eighth day, «it is fit» for sacrifice. «And it is written» subsequently in that verse: «“But from the eighth day and on it may be accepted» for an offering made by fire unto the Lord”; «consequently,» on the previous «night,» i.e., the night before the eighth day, «it is not» yet «fit.»

segments.he: הָא כֵּיצַד? לַיְלָה לִקְדוּשָּׁה, וְיוֹם לְהַרְצָאָה.
segments.en: «How» can «these» texts be reconciled? At «night» it is fit «for consecration, and» the following «day» it is fit «for effecting acceptance,» i.e., for sacrifice. Apparently, an offering that may be sacrificed the following day can be consecrated the previous night, even though it may not be sacrificed at night, and it is not considered an offering whose time has not yet arrived.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: לֵימָא קָסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים נִדְחִין?!
segments.en: § Rabbi Abbahu presumes that an animal consecrated before it may be sacrificed is disqualified. With regard to this, «Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Abbahu: Shall we say» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan holds» that consecrated «animals» that cannot be sacrificed at any given moment «are disqualified» from ever being sacrificed?

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין; דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בְּהֵמָה שֶׁל שְׁנֵי שׁוּתָּפִין – הִקְדִּישׁ חֶצְיָהּ, וְחָזַר וְלָקַח חֶצְיָהּ וְהִקְדִּישָׁהּ – קְדוֹשָׁה, וְאֵינָהּ קְרֵיבָה.
segments.en: Rabbi Abbahu «said to him: Yes, as Rabbi Yoḥanan says:» With regard to «an animal belonging to two partners,» if one of them «consecrated» the «half of it» that belongs to him, «and then purchased» the other «half of it» from his partner «and consecrated it, it is consecrated,» despite the fact that it was consecrated piecemeal. «But it may not be sacrificed,» since when he first consecrated it, the consecration did not extend to his partner’s half. Since the animal was not fit to be sacrificed then, it is disqualified permanently.

segments.he: וְעוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה, וּתְמוּרָתָהּ כְּיוֹצֵא בָּהּ.
segments.en: «But» as it is consecrated now, it can «render» consecrated as «a substitute» a non-sacred animal that is exchanged for it. If the owner substitutes a non-sacred animal for this one, the second animal becomes consecrated as well. «And» yet «its substitute is like it;» it too is consecrated but cannot be sacrificed.

segments.he: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ תְּלָת: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים נִדְחִין, וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ דָּחוּי מֵעִיקָּרָא הָוֵה דָּחוּי, וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
segments.en: «And» one can «conclude three» points «from» this statement: «Conclude from it» that «animals» that cannot be sacrificed «are» permanently «disqualified; and conclude from it» that «disqualification from the outset,» i.e., from the time the offering is consecrated, «is» permanent «disqualification; and conclude from it» that

segments.he: יֵשׁ דִּחוּי בְּדָמִים.
segments.en: «there is» permanent «disqualification» even «in» a case where the animal possesses sanctity that inheres in its «monetary» value, rather than inherent sanctity.

segments.he: אָמַר עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אָכַל חֵלֶב וְהִפְרִישׁ קׇרְבָּן, וְנִשְׁתַּמֵּד, וְחָזַר בּוֹ – הוֹאִיל וְנִדְחָה, יִדָּחֶה.
segments.en: § «Ulla says» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan says:» If one «ate» forbidden «fat and designated an offering» to atone for the transgression, «and» then «apostatized,» thereby disqualifying himself from bringing an offering, «and» later «recanted» his apostasy, «since» the offering was already «disqualified, it shall be disqualified» permanently.

segments.he: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אָכַל חֵלֶב וְהִפְרִישׁ קׇרְבָּן, וְנִשְׁתַּטָּה, וְחָזַר וְנִשְׁתַּפָּה – הוֹאִיל וְנִדְחָה, יִדָּחֶה.
segments.en: «It was also stated» that «Rabbi Yirmeya says» that «Rabbi Abbahu says» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan says:» If one «ate» forbidden «fat and designated an offering» to atone for his transgression, «and» then «became an imbecile,» who is unfit to bring an offering, «and» then «again became» halakhically «competent, since» the offering was already «disqualified, it shall be disqualified» permanently.

segments.he: וּצְרִיכִי; דְּאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן קַמַּיְיתָא – מִשּׁוּם דְּהוּא דָּחֵי נַפְשֵׁיהּ בְּיָדַיִם; אֲבָל הָכָא דְּמִמֵּילָא אִידְּחִי – כְּיָשֵׁן דָּמֵי.
segments.en: The Gemara notes: «And» both statements «are necessary. As, if» Rabbi Yoḥanan «had taught us» only «the first» statement, concerning an apostate, one might have reasoned that the offering is permanently disqualified «because he disqualified himself by» his own «action, but here,» in the case of one who became an imbecile, «where he was disqualified» through a process that occurs «by itself,» when he becomes competent again he may bring his sacrifice, as it is «considered as» though he were «asleep.» If one designated an offering and fell asleep, this certainly does not disqualify it.

segments.he: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן הָכָא – מִשּׁוּם דְּאֵין בְּיָדוֹ לַחֲזוֹר; אֲבָל הָכָא דְּיֵשׁ בְּיָדוֹ לַחֲזוֹר – אֵימָא לָא; צְרִיכָא.
segments.en: «And if» Rabbi Yoḥanan «had taught us» only the statement «here,» with regard to one who became an imbecile, one might have reasoned that the offering is permanently disqualified «because it is not in his power to return» to competence, «but here,» in the case of an apostate, «since it is in his power to recant» his apostasy, «I would say» that the offering is «not» permanently disqualified. Therefore, both statements are «necessary.»

segments.he: בָּעֵי רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: אָכַל חֵלֶב וְהִפְרִישׁ קׇרְבָּן, וְהוֹרוּ בֵּית דִּין שֶׁחֵלֶב מוּתָּר, וְחָזְרוּ בָּהֶן, מַהוּ? מִי הָוֵי דָּחוּי, אוֹ לָא הָוֵי דָּחוּי?
segments.en: «Rabbi Yirmeya raises a dilemma:» If one «ate» forbidden «fat and designated an offering» for the transgression, «and» then the «court ruled that» the type of «fat» he ate is «permitted,» thereby rendering the offering unnecessary, «and» the court subsequently «retracted» its ruling, in this case, «what is» the halakha? «Is» the offering permanently «disqualified, or is it not» permanently «disqualified?»

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא סָבָא: כִּי פָּתַח רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בִּדְחוּיִין – מֵהָא פָּתַח. מַאי טַעְמָא? הָתָם – גַּבְרָא אִידְּחִי, קׇרְבָּן לָא אִידְּחִי; הָכָא – קׇרְבָּן נָמֵי אִידְּחִי.
segments.en: «A certain elder [hahu sava] said to» Rabbi Yirmeya: «When Rabbi Yoḥanan introduced» the topic of permanently «disqualified» offerings, «he introduced» it «with this» case. «What is the reason? There,» in the case of one who apostatized or became an imbecile, although «the person was disqualified,» the «offering» itself «was not disqualified.» Consequently, it is less evident that the offering will be disqualified permanently. But «here,» in a case where the court ruled that the fat is permitted, the «offering» itself «was also disqualified,» as it was rendered unnecessary. Therefore, this is a more obvious example.
